title: Dedicated Burst Capacity — Burst Pool Rollout Plan (Regions + Hardware Order) (Draft)
content:
Audience
- Fleet/Infrastructure, SRE, Control Plane, Routing.
- Secondary: Product Dedicated (for launch sequencing) + CS (for customer comms timing).

Purpose
Draft rollout plan for Dedicated Burst Capacity burst pools by region + hardware class, including:
- region/hardware activation order
- capacity reservations + safety buffers
- gating criteria (technical + operational)
- rollback playbook pointers and concrete “what we do at 2am” switches

Non-goals
- Not a full sizing model (see sizing policy + sizing model v1).
- Not a customer selection doc (see PM beta customer selection ticket).

Definitions (short)
- Baseline: customer’s reserved Dedicated allocation.
- Burst: temporary additional capacity served from Redwood-managed shared burst pools in the same region + hardware class.
- Burst pool: segmented capacity slice (per region/hardware) used exclusively for burst traffic (never baseline).
- Fleet safety cap: global cap that can disable/restrict burst to protect platform-wide SLOs.

Key constraints (what drives the rollout)
1) Must not regress non-burst SLOs. Non-burst tenants are the protected class; burst is best-effort and should degrade before baseline.
2) Procurement lead times vary materially by region/hardware. We cannot commit to all regions at once.
3) Observability + denial reason codes must be ready before expanding beyond friendly beta.
4) We need deterministic admission behavior even under telemetry lag (beta issue; see hotfix notes).

Rollout principles
- Start with 1 region + 1 hardware class where we have the most predictable supply and strongest SRE coverage.
- Expand hardware classes within an already-enabled region before opening new regions (reduces variables).
- Expand regions only after we have at least 2 weeks of stable operation and one completed game day in production-like conditions.
- Keep pools small at first; scale pool size only after verifying neighbor impact metrics + billing reconciliation.

Proposed activation order (GA path)
Phase 0 — Internal + Friendly Beta (limited tenants, strict caps)
- us-east / H100
  - Rationale: highest capacity headroom + fastest on-call response + highest demand from Dedicated customers.
  - Pool segmentation: dedicated-burst-us-east-h100 (separate node labels + scheduler constraints).

Phase 1 — GA “Pilot Regions” (expand slowly, monitor regressions)
- us-east / H100 (GA)
- us-west / H100
- eu-west / L40S (if supply stable; otherwise defer to eu-west/H100)

Phase 2 — GA Expansion (after 4–6 weeks of stable pilot)
- eu-west / H100
- us-east / L40S
- us-west / L40S

Phase 3 — Broader Coverage (conditional, based on demand + supply)
- eu-central / H100 or L40S (decision depends on procurement + customer commitments)
- ap-southeast / L40S (only if we have local support + stable cross-AZ networking; no cross-region bursting in v1)

Notes
- We are explicitly not planning cross-region bursting in v1. Each region/hardware class is a self-contained SLO domain for burst.
- Hardware mapping is “class-based” (H100 vs L40S) and not SKU-specific; we should keep internal infra naming stable.

Capacity reservation policy (initial)
We need a consistent policy that avoids starving baseline Dedicated commitments.

Initial pool sizing targets (per region/hw)
- Start at: min(10% of regional Dedicated capacity for that hw class, OR N+2 nodes), whichever is smaller.
- Hard safety buffer: keep 20–30% unallocated headroom outside burst pools for baseline resiliency and incident handling.
- Regional supply risk multiplier:
  - us-east/us-west: 1.0x (lower risk)
  - eu-west: 1.2x (moderate risk)
  - eu-central/ap-southeast: 1.4x (higher risk)

Practical interpretation (what we do)
- For each region/hw, Fleet creates a “burst slice” with fixed node count at launch.
- Autoscaling within the slice is allowed only if it does not borrow from baseline-reserved pools and respects procurement constraints.
- Any “temporary borrow” from baseline pools is out of scope for v1.

Reserved capacity + procurement notes
- Burst pools should be treated as a product surface. We need predictable availability, so we should prefer reserved instances/long-lived nodes vs purely opportunistic.
- Before enabling a region/hw for GA, Fleet must confirm:
  - we can sustain the target pool size for 30 days without impacting baseline growth forecast
  - we have a 2–3 week lead plan for backfilling nodes if utilization exceeds target

Dependencies checklist (must be true before enabling any new region/hw)
Infra readiness
- Terraform module for burst pool provisioned in the target region/hw (node labels, taints, scheduling constraints, quotas).
- Pool is isolated from baseline (scheduler-level + quota-level separation).
- Circuit breaker paths validated (global + regional kill switch).

Control plane / routing readiness
- Region/hw allowlist toggle exists and is enforced at routing time.
- Admission controller deployed in-region (or with a documented, tested cross-AZ dependency model).
- Determinism guarantees: request retry behavior doesn’t cause oscillation in admission decisions.

Observability readiness
- Dashboards available:
  - pool saturation (GPU utilization, queue depth, admitted vs denied)
  - denial reason breakdown
  - neighbor impact indicators (non-burst p95/p99 deltas)
  - telemetry lag indicators
- Alerts configured + tuned (not paging on known-noisy panels, but paging on neighbor impact / SLO gate conditions).

Billing/metering readiness
- Meter export enabled and reconciles against raw counters.
- Idempotency handling validated (no double-billing on retries).
- Finance has a sample invoice line item from staging/prod-like validation.

Operational readiness
- Runbook reviewed by SRE on-call rotation (including “reduce caps” and “disable burst” steps).
- Support has denial reason code explainer (for 429s / overload messages) and escalation path.
- Game day executed for this region/hw OR executed for a substantially similar topology and re-validated via smoke test.

Gating criteria (what we measure to proceed)
Gates are evaluated per region/hw slice for 7 consecutive days (or longer if signal is noisy).

Gate A — Non-burst tenant protection (must pass)
- No sustained regression in protected SLOs for non-burst tenants attributable to burst activity:
  - Non-burst p95 latency delta: <= +5% vs baseline (rolling 1h windows) during burst windows
  - Non-burst error rate delta: <= +0.1% absolute increase (rolling 1h windows)
  - Tail amplification alarm (p99) not triggered more than 1x/day and must auto-clear
- If breached: hold expansion, reduce caps, or disable burst (see rollback).

Gate B — Burst stability + predictability (must pass)
- Admission controller availability >= 99.9% in the target region/hw.
- Admission decision latency within expected bounds (p99 under internal threshold; see service SLO).
- Denials are explainable: >= 95% of denials carry a non-“unknown” reason code.

Gate C — Saturation behavior is safe (must pass)
- Under load test or real burst spikes, the system degrades by denying burst rather than harming baseline.
- Queue/backpressure behaves as designed (no cascading timeouts into routing).

Gate D — Metering correctness (must pass)
- Daily reconciliation: metered burst usage within +/- 1% of raw counters, and no systematic skew by tenant.
- No open P0/P1 issues related to double-counting on retries.

Gate E — Operational readiness (must pass)
- On-call can identify and mitigate overload within 15 minutes (validated in game day or incident drill).
- Kill switch propagation tested (global and region/hw) and documented.

Rollout timeline (current working draft)
- Week 0: us-east/H100 internal dogfood, strict caps, limited tenants (internal + 1–3 friendly).
- Week 2: us-east/H100 beta expansion to 5–8 tenants; introduce limited “silver” tier.
- Week 4: us-east/H100 GA pilot (still with conservative defaults).
- Week 6: us-west/H100 enablement.
- Week 8: eu-west (L40S or H100, supply-dependent).

This is subject to procurement changes. We should not externally commit to specific region dates until Gate D is green (metering) and Gate A has at least 7 clean days.

Rollout mechanics (how we turn things on)
We need to avoid manual snowflakes; toggles should be consistent:
1) Provision burst pool infra for region/hw (Terraform apply + verify nodes registered).
2) Enable region/hw allowlist at control plane (feature flag). Keep tenant allowlist empty initially.
3) Turn on admission controller integration in routing for that region/hw (shadow mode first if available; otherwise low traffic).
4) Add 1 internal tenant (dogfood) with low max burst ratio and tight per-tenant cap.
5) Gradually add tenants + expand caps.
6) Promote to GA once gating criteria are green.

Suggested default caps for initial GA (subject to final PRD)
- Max burst ratio: 1.5x baseline
- Per-tenant burst cap: min(25% of pool, absolute cap in GPUs, whichever lower)
- Cooldown: 10 minutes after sustained saturation event (prevents thrash)
- Priority tiers: allow “gold” only when pool headroom exists; ensure anti-starvation rule enabled

Rollback plan (what we do when things go wrong)
Severity levels
- P0: non-burst SLO regression or fleet safety cap triggered; immediate action required.
- P1: widespread admission errors/timeouts or unknown denials; action required within the hour.

Rollback levers (ordered by blast radius)
1) Reduce per-tenant cap (no code deploy; config-only)
- Use when: pool saturated and a few tenants are dominating.
- Expected effect: more burst denials for those tenants, minimal baseline impact.

2) Reduce max burst ratio globally for region/hw
- Use when: neighbor impact indicators move but are not yet paging.

3) Disable burst for specific tenant(s)
- Use when: a single tenant’s burst pattern is pathological (e.g., retry storms, huge batch jobs).

4) Disable region/hw allowlist (turn off burst in that slice)
- Use when: systemic issue in that region/hw (admission controller instability, telemetry lag, routing integration bug).

5) Global circuit breaker (fleet safety cap)
- Use when: signs of platform-wide impact or multi-region correlated degradation.

Operational pointers
- Primary runbook: Burst Pool Overload Mitigation Runbook (Confluence).
- Pager annotations: include “what switch did we flip” and “what tenants were bursting” in incident timeline.
- Communication: if we disable burst, notify CS + impacted tenants with clear denial reason messaging (burst is best-effort).

Open questions / TODOs
- Finalize eu-west hardware choice for Phase 1 (L40S vs H100): depends on procurement confirmation + expected customer demand mix.
- Confirm the minimum viable pool size per region/hw (N+2 is a placeholder; needs to align with failure domain assumptions).
- Decide whether ap-southeast is worth enabling in 2025H2 for v1; depends on support and networking reliability.
- Align on the exact Gate A thresholds with SRE (are +5% p95 and +0.1% error delta the right numbers?).
- Validate kill switch propagation time end-to-end (control plane -> routing -> admission controller).

Appendix: quick “go/no-go” checklist for enabling a new region/hw
Go only if all are true:
- [ ] Infra provisioned and isolated from baseline
- [ ] Routing integration deployed and tested
- [ ] Admission controller healthy (SLO met)
- [ ] Dashboards + alerts exist and on-call reviewed
- [ ] Metering reconciliation is green
- [ ] Game day (or equivalent drill) completed
- [ ] Rollback levers verified in staging + one production smoke test

Owner notes (Vanessa)
- Please leave comments directly in this doc with region/hw concerns (especially procurement constraints and any “this will never work in region X” issues).
- I’m tracking final proposed region sequence for GA in the Fleet weekly capacity review once we have 2 weeks of us-east/H100 beta data.
